rationale: Builds directly on the current best reverse-tail recurrent baseline with a compact structural change instead of another scalar sweep. The recurrent tail now lightly refreshes its decoder-output anchor after each reverse revisit, so later recurrent passes chase a partially updated target rather than a frozen one. This spends no meaningful extra bytes, keeps shapes and compile behavior stable on MLX, and targets the still-promising reverse-tail anchor family without repeating the heavier curriculum and loss-alignment experiments that recently collapsed.
title: Light Reverse-Tail Anchor Refresh
